Q: Bash function: redirect command output to file but keep function printf output on stdout A:

If I call it like this:

execute_command_with_progress_bar ssh root@"$DEV_IP_ADDR" ls >> ./results.log 2>&1">

Then everything goes into results.log (content of remote ls) and all printfs in the execute_command_with_progress_bar function.

Well, yes. If you perform such redirections on the function call then they apply to everything in the function body, except where additionally redirected. You have no easy way inside the function to reverse that, because it has no open file descriptor for the original standard output. The solution I would recommend is to rely on the function to do redirection internally, instead of redirecting the call.

There are lots of ways you could implement that, from communicating details via shell variables to making the function recognize options to tell it what you want. Perhaps you would end up with calls like so:

execute_command_with_progress_bar -o ./results.log --redirect-stderr -- ssh root@"$DEV_IP_ADDR" ls

Then the function might do something along these lines:

execute_command_with_progress_bar() {
  # process options or whatever ...

  (
    # The following redirections are scoped to this subshell:
    [[ -n "$stdout_file" ]] && exec 1>"$stdout_file"
    [[ -n "$redirect_stderr" ]] && exec 2>&1

    "$@"
  )

  # monitoring / progress reporting ...
}

Q: Code to select cell based on cell address input by user A:

You will get more-useful responses here if you could add a little more context around the bigger picture of what want to do. Eg. what is the purpose of selecting the cell? So you can copy it, or just to "show" it to the user? If it's just to copy it then there's no need to select it.

For example:

Sub SelectCellBasedonUserInput()

    Dim wksCellstoCopy As Worksheet
    Dim wksCopiedData As Worksheet
    Dim CopyCell As String, CopyWks As String
    
    Set wksCellstoCopy = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("Cells to Copy")
    Set wksCopiedData = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("Copied Data")
    
    CopyWks = wksCellstoCopy.Range("A2").Value
    CopyCell = wksCellstoCopy.Range("C2").Value
    
    'go to the sheet and seelct the range
    With ThisWorkbook.Worksheets(CopyWks)
        .Select
        .Range(CopyCell).Select
    End With
    
    '...or if you just want to copy the cell
    ThisWorkbook.Worksheets(CopyWks).Range(CopyCell).Copy
    
End Sub
